name: Shelter_Weather_Interaction
description: How storms, wind, temperature, and precipitation affect shelter structural integrity and habitability.

questions.question: Does storm damage to shelters teach real structural engineering principles like wind load and stress concentration?
questions.answer: Yes. Shelters facing storm wind take damage on windward faces first. Corner joints fail under repeated stress, teaching real failure modes.

questions.question: Can players learn about wind load, stress concentration, and fatigue cycles by observing shelter failure patterns?
questions.answer: Yes. Damage accumulates at joints and unsupported spans first. Players learn that repeated minor storms fatigue materials faster than one big storm.

questions.question: Does shelter positioning relative to terrain teach microclimate awareness and wind-shadow principles?
questions.answer: Yes. A shelter in the lee of a ridge takes less wind damage. Canyon shelters experience wind funneling. Players learn terrain meteorology.

questions.question: Can players learn to predict weather by observing predictive visual cues (cloud formations, wind changes, pressure drops)?
questions.answer: Yes. Approaching storms have visual precursors. Players who read these signs can reinforce shelters or evacuate before the storm hits.

questions.question: Is dynamic storm damage with physics-based shelter destruction a shareable, viral-worthy moment?
questions.answer: Yes. A storm ripping the roof off a poorly built shelter while the player scrambles to repair is a highly shareable emergent moment.

questions.question: Does surviving a named storm inside a player-built shelter create lasting memorable gameplay stories?
questions.answer: Yes. Surviving a category-5 storm because of smart material choices creates a narrative the player will retell.

questions.question: Can weather-driven shelter interaction differentiate our game from survival games with static bases?
questions.answer: Yes. Most survival games have indestructible player bases. Ours make shelter a dynamic, vulnerable system that requires maintenance.

questions.question: Does visible shelter damage accumulation (cracks, holes, warped frames) drive emotional attachment and urgency?
questions.answer: Yes. Watching your shelter deteriorate creates maintenance urgency and makes each storm feel threatening.

questions.question: Do different storm types (sandstorm, blizzard, electrical storm, acid rain) have distinct visual and physical damage profiles?
questions.answer: Yes. Sandstorms abrade surfaces. Blizzards load roofs with snow weight. Acid rain degrades materials chemically. Each requires different countermeasures.

questions.question: Does wind direction relative to shelter orientation affect which modules take damage first?
questions.answer: Yes. Windward modules take damage first. Leeward modules are partially protected. A rotated shelter survives a directional storm better.

questions.question: Can players forecast incoming severe weather using visual cues (cloud formation, wind speed, atmospheric glow)?
questions.answer: Yes. Weather has build-up phases with distinct skybox and particle changes. Players learn to read these signs.

questions.question: Does accumulated damage affect shelter habitability (drafts, leaks, temperature loss) before structural failure?
questions.answer: Yes. A cracked module leaks heat and lets in precipitation. The player feels the consequence before total collapse.

questions.question: Can weather-shelter interaction reuse the existing planetary weather system's storm events and wind vectors?
questions.answer: Yes. The weather system already produces storms and wind vectors. Shelter interaction consumes these as damage inputs.

questions.question: Is shelter damage accumulation simulation cheap enough for real-time updates on the RTX 3060?
questions.answer: Yes. Damage is a per-module float updated on weather tick (every 5-10s). No per-frame physics needed for accumulation.

questions.question: Can a basic storm-damage demo (wind applies damage to windward module, visual cracking) be built in one day?
questions.answer: Yes. Wind vector dot-product with module face, damage accumulation, and material parameter blend for cracking texture can be prototyped in 6 hours.

questions.question: Does shelter damage state persist correctly across save/load cycles?
questions.answer: Yes. Per-module damage percentage, accumulated weather exposure, and repair state serialize to the save game JSON.

questions.question: Does the game code generator need templates for damage state visualization components and weather interaction handlers?
questions.answer: Yes. A shelter damage component (health, damage type, visual state) and a weather interaction interface need generator templates.

questions.question: Can weather interaction (storm applies damage, shelter degrades) be verified via automated sleepwalker sim?
questions.answer: Yes. Sleepwalker can place a known shelter, trigger a storm, wait N ticks, and query per-module damage values.

questions.question: Is damage accumulation easily implementable as material health points consumed by weather events?
questions.answer: Yes. Each module has (max_health, current_health, damage_rate_per_storm_class). Weather reduces health. Repair restores it.

questions.question: Can damage thresholds (crack at 75%, leak at 50%, collapse at 0%) be balanced via data tables?
questions.answer: Yes. Damage thresholds, repair costs, and weather resistance are data-driven per material and per module type.

questions.question: Does weather interaction depend on the planetary weather system being fully operational?
questions.answer: Yes. Shelter interaction requires storm events, wind vectors, and precipitation data from the active weather system.

questions.question: Does this prove that survival mechanics can meaningfully interact with environmental systems (not just exist alongside them)?
questions.answer: Yes. Shelter-weather interaction proves the environment directly affects player-built structures, not just the player character.

questions.question: Was this sub-feature derived from Shelter_Habitat question 9 (weather physically affects shelter integrity)?
questions.answer: Yes. Shelter_Habitat Q9 establishes that storms damage weak structures, which requires detailed weather-shelter interaction to implement.

questions.question: Does real-time physics-based shelter deformation during storms conflict with the 30+ fps performance target?
questions.answer: Minor conflict. Full deformable mesh physics is expensive. Use material parameter blending for visual damage, not vertex deformation.

questions.question: What UE5 physics and weather knowledge is required for implementing storm damage on shelters?
questions.answer: UE5 weather system API, material parameter collections, per-actor damage component pattern, and data-driven material resistance.

questions.question: Does teaching weather science and structural meteorology through shelter gameplay serve the educational RPG vision?
questions.answer: Yes. Weather-shelter interaction teaches real meteorology and structural engineering. This directly serves the educational mission.
